# Objective and acceptance target

The empty-section gate must reject a handoff whose body sections are present but
hollow. Acceptance is a mutation test: deleting the gate has to make the suite
fail, not pass quietly.

# Confirmed facts and read set

Read `schemas/handoff.schema.json` and `bin/agent-handoff`. The gate lives in
`section_is_substantive` and is called from `check_doctor`. No other caller
exists, confirmed by grep across the tree.

# Completed

Added the `section_is_substantive` check and wired it into `check_doctor` in
`bin/agent-handoff`. Added the mutation test at
`tests/test_workspace.py::test_hollow_section_is_rejected`.

# Current operation

The gate passes its own mutation test. Not yet run against a real repository
with an unclean worktree, which is the next thing to check.

# Exact next action

Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -k hollow` and confirm the
empty-section gate still fails the suite when deleted.

# Decisions/spec/plan changes

Chose a character-count floor of 24 over a word-count floor, because a floor in
characters is stable across languages and does not need a tokenizer. Recorded
in `docs/STANDARD.md` under section 4.

# Validation evidence

RUN-0001: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` returned `OK` with 67 tests.
`python3 bin/agent-handoff doctor --strict` returned 0 errors and 0 warnings
against a freshly initialised workspace.

# Blockers and questions

none — no open blockers. One open question for the maintainer: whether the
character floor should be configurable per project or stay fixed at 24.

# Do not repeat / safe shortcuts

Do not re-derive that the gate is reachable from `check_doctor`; it is, and the
grep is in the read set. Do not raise `HANDOFF_MIN_BODY` to make a specific
handoff pass — that weakens every future gate.

# Stale or contradictory information

An earlier note claimed the doctor auto-fixed empty sections. It does not and
never did; the doctor is read-only by contract.

# Working tree and uncommitted paths

Clean at the time of writing. `git status --porcelain` returned no output and
`git rev-parse HEAD` matched the checkpoint commit above. A dirty tree would
have made this checkpoint `provisional-dirty`, which claims the diff is
captured and recoverable rather than assuming it is.
